items.question: Maa has a small roti with 10 equal pieces and a big roti with 16 equal pieces. Every piece is the same size. Is 1/2 of the small roti the same amount as 1/2 of the big roti? Then compare 1/2 and 1/4 of two rotis of the same size, each cut into 12 equal pieces.
steps: The small roti has 10 pieces. Half of 10 is 10 ÷ 2 = 5, so 1/2 of the small roti is 5 pieces.
The big roti has 16 pieces. Half of 16 is 16 ÷ 2 = 8, so 1/2 of the big roti is 8 pieces.
Both amounts are called 1/2, but 5 pieces and 8 pieces are not the same amount. The wholes are different sizes.
Now take two rotis of the same size, each with 12 pieces. 1/2 of 12 is 12 ÷ 2 = 6 pieces.
1/4 of 12 is 12 ÷ 4 = 3 pieces.
6 pieces are more than 3 pieces, so on the same whole 1/2 is more than 1/4.
Check: the pieces of both rotis are the same size, so 6 pieces really is more than 3 pieces.
items.answer: No. 1/2 of the small roti is 5 pieces and 1/2 of the big roti is 8 pieces, because the wholes are different sizes. On the same whole, 1/2 (6 pieces) is more than 1/4 (3 pieces)

videos.answer: No. 1/2 of the small roti is 5 pieces and 1/2 of the big roti is 8 pieces, because the wholes are different sizes. On the same whole, 1/2 (6 pieces) is more than 1/4 (3 pieces)

source: Tamanna's Chocolates: is she correct

items.question: Tamanna is a student of Grade 5. She has two chocolates of different sizes. She says that 1/3 of one of her chocolates is bigger than 1/2 of the other chocolate. Is that correct? Explain why this is so.
steps: Count the blocks. The small bar has 4 blocks, 2 rows of 2. The big bar has 9 blocks, 3 rows of 3. Every block is the same size.
Take 1/2 of the small bar: share 4 blocks into 2 equal groups, 4 ÷ 2 = 2 blocks.
Take 1/3 of the big bar: share 9 blocks into 3 equal groups, 9 ÷ 3 = 3 blocks.
3 blocks are more than 2 blocks, so 1/3 of the big bar is bigger than 1/2 of the small bar.
This happens because the two bars are different sizes. A fraction is a part of its own whole.
Check: the blocks are all the same size, so 3 blocks really is more chocolate than 2 blocks.
items.answer: Yes, she is correct for these two chocolates. 1/3 of the big bar is 3 blocks and 1/2 of the small bar is 2 blocks, because the two wholes are different sizes.

videos.answer: Yes, she is correct for these two chocolates. 1/3 of the big bar is 3 blocks and 1/2 of the small bar is 2 blocks, because the two wholes are different sizes.

source: Tamanna's Chocolates: when is 1/2 more than 1/3

items.question: When can we say that 1/2 of something is greater than 1/3 of something?
steps: 1/2 and 1/3 are parts of a whole. A fraction always belongs to its own whole.
Take two bars of the same size, each with 6 blocks.
1/2 of 6 blocks is 6 ÷ 2 = 3 blocks.
1/3 of 6 blocks is 6 ÷ 3 = 2 blocks.
3 blocks are more than 2 blocks, so when both are parts of the same whole, 1/2 is greater than 1/3.
If the wholes are different sizes the answer can change: in Tamanna's bars, 1/3 of the big bar was 3 blocks and 1/2 of the small bar was 2 blocks.
Check: the rule is that the wholes must be the same.
items.answer: When both fractions are parts of the same whole, that is, two wholes of the same size, 1/2 is greater than 1/3. If the wholes are different sizes we cannot say.

videos.answer: When both fractions are parts of the same whole, that is, two wholes of the same size, 1/2 is greater than 1/3. If the wholes are different sizes we cannot say.

items.question: A grid has 3 columns and 7 rows of equal squares. Find 1/3 of the grid and 1/7 of the grid.
steps: Count the squares: 3 × 7 = 21 squares in all.
1/3 means 3 equal groups. Share 21 squares: 21 ÷ 3 = 7 squares in each group.
One group is 1/3 of the grid, so 1/3 of the grid is 7 squares, for example one whole column.
1/7 means 7 equal groups. Share 21 squares: 21 ÷ 7 = 3 squares in each group.
One group is 1/7 of the grid, so 1/7 of the grid is 3 squares, for example one whole row.
Check: 3 groups of 7 squares make 3 × 7 = 21, and 7 groups of 3 squares make 7 × 3 = 21.
items.answer: 1/3 of the grid is 7 squares and 1/7 of the grid is 3 squares

videos.answer: 1/3 of the grid is 7 squares and 1/7 of the grid is 3 squares

source: A grid has 6 columns and 4 rows of equal squares. Show that

items.question: A grid has 6 columns and 4 rows of equal squares. Show that 3 pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/8 of the grid, and find how many pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/12 of the grid.
steps: Count the squares: 6 × 4 = 24 squares in all, so each square is 1/24 of the grid.
1/8 of the grid is 24 ÷ 8 = 3 squares.
Shade 3 squares, one at a time. 3 pieces of 1/24 shade 3 squares, the same area as 1/8, so 3/24 = 1/8.
1/12 of the grid is 24 ÷ 12 = 2 squares.
2 pieces of 1/24 shade 2 squares, the same area as 1/12, so 2/24 = 1/12.
Check: 8 groups of 3 squares make 8 × 3 = 24, and 12 groups of 2 squares make 12 × 2 = 24.
items.answer: 3 pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/8 (3/24 = 1/8), and 2 pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/12 (2/24 = 1/12)

videos.answer: 3 pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/8 (3/24 = 1/8), and 2 pieces of 1/24 shade the same area as 1/12 (2/24 = 1/12)

source: Playing with a Grid: shade the three grids

items.question: Shade 1/8 of Grid A in red. Shade 1/6 of Grid B in blue. Shade 1/12 of Grid C in yellow.
steps: Each grid has 8 columns and 6 rows, so there are 8 × 6 = 48 squares.
Grid A: 1/8 means 8 equal groups. 48 ÷ 8 = 6 squares in one group. Shade 6 squares red.
Grid B: 1/6 means 6 equal groups. 48 ÷ 6 = 8 squares in one group. Shade 8 squares blue.
Grid C: 1/12 means 12 equal groups. 48 ÷ 12 = 4 squares in one group. Shade 4 squares yellow.
Check: 8 groups of 6 squares make 8 × 6 = 48, 6 groups of 8 squares make 6 × 8 = 48, and 12 groups of 4 squares make 12 × 4 = 48.
items.answer: Grid A: 6 squares in red. Grid B: 8 squares in blue. Grid C: 4 squares in yellow. Your squares may be in different places.

videos.answer: Grid A: 6 squares in red. Grid B: 8 squares in blue. Grid C: 4 squares in yellow. Your squares may be in different places.

source: Playing with a Grid: find 1/3

items.question: Do you see 1/3 in any of the grids? Mark it.
steps: 1/3 of 48 squares is 48 ÷ 3 = 16 squares. Look for 16 squares made of whole parts.
Grid A is cut into parts of 1/8, with 6 squares in each part. Joining them gives 6, 12 or 18 squares, never 16. So 1/3 is not made from the parts of Grid A.
Grid B has parts of 1/6 with 8 squares each. 2 × 8 = 16, so 2 parts of 1/6 make 16 squares. 2/6 = 1/3. Mark 2 parts in Grid B.
Grid C has parts of 1/12 with 4 squares each. 4 × 4 = 16, so 4 parts of 1/12 make 16 squares. 4/12 = 1/3. Mark 4 parts in Grid C.
Check: 2/6 = 1/3 and 4/12 = 1/3, and both are 16 squares out of 48.
items.answer: Yes, in Grid B and Grid C. In Grid B, 2 parts of 1/6 make 16 squares. In Grid C, 4 parts of 1/12 make 16 squares. Joining the parts of 1/8 in Grid A gives 6, 12 or 18 squares, never 16.

videos.answer: Yes, in Grid B and Grid C. In Grid B, 2 parts of 1/6 make 16 squares. In Grid C, 4 parts of 1/12 make 16 squares. Joining the parts of 1/8 in Grid A gives 6, 12 or 18 squares, never 16.

items.question: A circle is cut into equal pieces of 1/4. How many pieces make the whole circle? Then the circle is cut into equal pieces of 1/8. How many pieces make the whole?
steps: A piece of 1/4 is one of 4 equal parts of the circle.
To fill the circle we need all 4 parts, so we need 4 pieces of 1/4.
4 pieces of 1/4 make 4/4 = 1 whole circle.
A piece of 1/8 is one of 8 equal parts of the circle. We need all 8 parts, so we need 8 pieces of 1/8.
8 pieces of 1/8 make 8/8 = 1 whole circle.
Check: the bottom number tells how many equal pieces the whole has, so it is also the number of pieces we need: 4 for 1/4 and 8 for 1/8.
items.answer: 4 pieces of 1/4 make a whole, and 8 pieces of 1/8 make a whole

videos.answer: 4 pieces of 1/4 make a whole, and 8 pieces of 1/8 make a whole

source: A circle is made with one piece of 1/2, one piece of 1/4 and

items.question: A circle is made with one piece of 1/2, one piece of 1/4 and two pieces of 1/8. Show that these pieces make a whole. Then show that a piece of 1/8 can be covered by two pieces of 1/16, and write the two names.
steps: Rename every piece with the bottom number 8 and count: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + 1/8 = 4/8 + 2/8 + 1/8 + 1/8.
Count the pieces of 1/8: 4 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 8, so the pieces make 8/8 = 1 whole.
Now break one piece of 1/8 into 2 equal parts. Each part is a piece of 1/16.
2 pieces of 1/16 cover exactly the same part as 1 piece of 1/8, so 1/8 = 2/16.
Check: 8 pieces of 1/8 make a whole and 16 pieces of 1/16 make a whole. Each piece of 1/8 holds 2 pieces of 1/16, and 8 × 2 = 16.
items.answer: The pieces make 8/8 = 1 whole, and 1/8 = 2/16, two names for the same part

videos.answer: The pieces make 8/8 = 1 whole, and 1/8 = 2/16, two names for the same part

source: A strip has 20 equal parts. How many pieces of 1/20 fit insi

items.question: A strip has 20 equal parts. How many pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/4 of the strip? How many fit inside 1/10 of the strip?
steps: One piece of 1/20 is 1 of the 20 equal parts, because 20 ÷ 20 = 1.
1/4 of the strip is 20 ÷ 4 = 5 parts.
5 parts are covered by 5 pieces of 1/20, so 5 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/4.
1/10 of the strip is 20 ÷ 10 = 2 parts.
2 parts are covered by 2 pieces of 1/20, so 2 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/10.
Check: 4 pieces of 5 parts fill the strip, 4 × 5 = 20, and 10 pieces of 2 parts fill it, 10 × 2 = 20.
items.answer: 5 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/4 (5/20 = 1/4), and 2 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/10 (2/20 = 1/10)

videos.answer: 5 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/4 (5/20 = 1/4), and 2 pieces of 1/20 fit inside 1/10 (2/20 = 1/10)

source: Fun with Fraction Kit: the shaded strip

items.question: Is 1/3 equal to 2/6? Let us find out. Look at the picture and identify the fractions. Are there two different ways to write the fraction represented by the shaded part? ___
steps: The strip has 6 equal parts and 2 of them are shaded, so the shaded part is 2/6.
Group the 6 parts into groups of 2: 6 ÷ 2 = 3 groups.
The 2 shaded parts are 1 of the 3 equal groups, so the shaded part is also 1/3.
The same shaded part is written in two ways: 2/6 and 1/3.
Check: 3 groups of 2 parts make 3 × 2 = 6 parts, so 2/6 = 1/3.
items.answer: Yes. The shaded part is 2/6 and also 1/3, so 1/3 = 2/6.

videos.answer: Yes. The shaded part is 2/6 and also 1/3, so 1/3 = 2/6.

5 pieces of 1/5 make 5/5 = 1 whole.
items.answer: 5 pieces of 1/5 make a whole.

source: Fun with Fraction Kit: equivalents of 1/2

items.question: What else is equivalent to 1/2? 1/2 = 2/4 = ___ = ___ = ___
steps: The kit shows 1/2 = 2/4: 2 pieces of 1/4 fill the piece of 1/2.
Try pieces of 1/6: 3 pieces of 1/6 fill the piece of 1/2, so 1/2 = 3/6.
Try pieces of 1/8: 4 pieces of 1/8 fill the piece of 1/2, so 1/2 = 4/8.
Try pieces of 1/12: 6 pieces of 1/12 fill the piece of 1/2, so 1/2 = 6/12.
Check: in each name the top number is half of the bottom number: 2 and 4, 3 and 6, 4 and 8, 6 and 12.
items.answer: Sample answer: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8 = 6/12. Your answer may differ, other equivalent fractions are also right.

videos.answer: Sample answer: 1/2 = 2/4 = 3/6 = 4/8 = 6/12. Your answer may differ, other equivalent fractions are also right.

source: Let Us Do (fraction kit), Q1

items.question: In groups of 3 or 4, find different ways of making a whole with different fraction pieces from your kit. Write the equivalent fractions for the following that you may find in the process. (a): 1/3 = ___ = ___ = ___; (b): 1/4 = ___ = ___ = ___; (c): 1/5 = ___ = ___ = ___; (d): 1/6 = ___ = ___ = ___
steps: Fill each piece with smaller pieces and count them. The count is the top number of the new name. The kit gives some names, and the rest come from cutting every part into more equal parts.
(a): 2 pieces of 1/6 fill 1/3, and 4 pieces of 1/12 fill 1/3. Cutting each third into 3 equal parts gives 3/9. So 1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9 = 4/12.
(b): 2 pieces of 1/8 fill 1/4, and 3 pieces of 1/12 fill 1/4. Cutting each fourth into 4 equal parts gives 4/16. So 1/4 = 2/8 = 3/12 = 4/16.
(c): Cutting each fifth into 2, 3 and 4 equal parts gives 2/10, 3/15 and 4/20. So 1/5 = 2/10 = 3/15 = 4/20.
(d): 2 pieces of 1/12 fill 1/6. Cutting each sixth into 3 and 4 equal parts gives 3/18 and 4/24. So 1/6 = 2/12 = 3/18 = 4/24.
Check one name from each part: 2/6 = 1/3, 2/8 = 1/4, 2/10 = 1/5 and 2/12 = 1/6.

source: Let Us Do (fraction kit), Q2 A

items.question: Find the following using your kit. You can also shade and check by shading. A. How many pieces of 1/6 make 1/3? The shaded part is 1/3. Identify 1/6 in the same whole and find how many pieces of 1/6 fit into 1/3.
steps: The whole has 6 equal squares, so each square is 1/6 of the whole.
The shaded part is 1/3. It is the first column of 2 squares.
Each square is a piece of 1/6, so 2 pieces of 1/6 fit into 1/3.
Check: 3 columns of 2 squares make 3 × 2 = 6 squares, so 2/6 = 1/3.
items.answer: 2 pieces of 1/6 make 1/3.

videos.answer: 2 pieces of 1/6 make 1/3.

source: Let Us Do (fraction kit), Q3

items.question: Do as instructed using your fraction kit. Make a whole using only 1/6 and 1/12 pieces. Make a whole using 1/12, 1/4, and 1/2 pieces. Make a whole using any five pieces of the same size. Make a whole using any seven pieces. Play in a group with this kit and find other interesting combinations to make a whole. Write or draw your findings.
steps: First task, only pieces of 1/6 and 1/12: take 3 pieces of 1/6 and 6 pieces of 1/12. 3/6 = 6/12, so 3/6 + 6/12 = 6/12 + 6/12 = 12/12 = 1.
Second task, pieces of 1/12, 1/4 and 1/2: take one piece of 1/2, one piece of 1/4 and 3 pieces of 1/12. 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/12 + 1/12 + 1/12 = 6/12 + 3/12 + 3/12 = 12/12 = 1.
Third task, five pieces of the same size: take five pieces of 1/5. 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5 = 5/5 = 1.
Fourth task, any seven pieces: take two pieces of 1/4, one piece of 1/6 and four pieces of 1/12. 2 + 1 + 4 = 7 pieces. In twelfths, 6/12 + 2/12 + 4/12 = 12/12 = 1.
Your own findings: any pieces that add up to 12/12 make a whole. For example one piece each of 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6: 1/2 + 1/3 + 1/6 = 6/12 + 4/12 + 2/12 = 12/12 = 1.
Check: every whole adds up to 12/12 or 5/5, which is 1, so there is no gap and no overlap.
items.answer: Sample answer: first, 3 pieces of 1/6 and 6 pieces of 1/12. Second, one piece each of 1/2 and 1/4 and 3 pieces of 1/12. Third, five pieces of 1/5. Fourth, two pieces of 1/4, one piece of 1/6 and four pieces of 1/12. Your own: 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6. Each makes 1 whole. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: first, 3 pieces of 1/6 and 6 pieces of 1/12. Second, one piece each of 1/2 and 1/4 and 3 pieces of 1/12. Third, five pieces of 1/5. Fourth, two pieces of 1/4, one piece of 1/6 and four pieces of 1/12. Your own: 1/2, 1/3 and 1/6. Each makes 1 whole. Your answer may differ.

items.question: A bar is cut into 5 equal parts and 4 parts are shaded, so 4/5 of the bar is shaded. Now cut every part into 2 equal pieces. What fraction names the shaded part now? Has the shaded area changed?
steps: The bar has 5 equal parts and 4 of them are shaded, so the shaded part is 4/5.
Cut every part into 2 equal pieces. The whole now has 5 × 2 = 10 equal parts.
Each shaded part was cut into 2 pieces, so the shaded pieces are 4 × 2 = 8.
8 shaded pieces out of 10 equal pieces is the fraction 8/10.
Check the area: nothing was added to the colour and nothing was taken away. Only cut lines were drawn, so the shaded area is the same.
The same part of the whole has two names, 4/5 and 8/10. They are equivalent fractions.
items.answer: 8/10. The shaded area has not changed, so 4/5 = 8/10

videos.answer: 8/10. The shaded area has not changed, so 4/5 = 8/10

source: A bar has 8 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded, so 3/8 of th

items.question: A bar has 8 equal parts and 3 parts are shaded, so 3/8 of the bar is shaded. Cut every part into 2 equal pieces, and then, on a copy of the first bar, cut every part into 3 equal pieces. Write the two new fractions and find the pattern.
steps: The bar has 8 equal parts and 3 are shaded: 3/8.
Cut every part into 2 equal pieces. The shaded pieces are 3 × 2 = 6. The equal pieces in the whole are 8 × 2 = 16. The fraction is 6/16.
Cut every part of the first bar into 3 equal pieces. The shaded pieces are 3 × 3 = 9. The equal pieces in the whole are 8 × 3 = 24. The fraction is 9/24.
Look at the top numbers: 3, 6, 9. Look at the bottom numbers: 8, 16, 24.
From 3/8 to 6/16 the top and the bottom were both multiplied by 2. From 3/8 to 9/24 they were both multiplied by 3.
Check: the shaded area is the same in all three bars, so 3/8 = 6/16 = 9/24.
items.answer: 3/8 = 6/16 = 9/24. To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top number and the bottom number by the same number

videos.answer: 3/8 = 6/16 = 9/24. To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top number and the bottom number by the same number

source: Making Equivalent Fractions: equivalents of 1/3

items.question: Sameer has shaded one-third of the figures. He draws horizontal lines to divide the shapes into more equal parts. Divide the wholes given below into more equal parts and find fractions equivalent to 1/3. Write them in the boxes below the images. 1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9 = 4/12 = ___ = ___ = ___ = ___/24 = ___/36
steps: The shaded part is 1/3: the middle strip of 3 equal strips. Sameer cut each strip into 2, 3 and 4 pieces. The three empty boxes continue with 5, 6 and 7 pieces.
Cut each strip into 5 pieces. The whole has 3 × 5 = 15 pieces and the shaded strip has 1 × 5 = 5 pieces. The fraction is 5/15.
Cut each strip into 6 pieces. The whole has 3 × 6 = 18 pieces and the shaded strip has 1 × 6 = 6 pieces. The fraction is 6/18.
Cut each strip into 7 pieces. The whole has 3 × 7 = 21 pieces and the shaded strip has 1 × 7 = 7 pieces. The fraction is 7/21.
For ___/24, the bottom must be 24. Each strip is cut into 8 pieces, because 3 × 8 = 24. The top is 1 × 8 = 8, so the fraction is 8/24.
For ___/36, each strip is cut into 12 pieces, because 3 × 12 = 36. The top is 1 × 12 = 12, so the fraction is 12/36.
Check: the bottom number is always 3 times the top number. 3 × 12 = 36, and the same is true for 6/18 and 8/24.
items.answer: Sample answer: 1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9 = 4/12 = 5/15 = 6/18 = 7/21 = 8/24 = 12/36. The three open blanks may be filled with other equivalent fractions, but the two boxes must be 8 and 12. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: 1/3 = 2/6 = 3/9 = 4/12 = 5/15 = 6/18 = 7/21 = 8/24 = 12/36. The three open blanks may be filled with other equivalent fractions, but the two boxes must be 8 and 12. Your answer may differ.

source: Making Equivalent Fractions: equivalents of 2/5

items.question: The below pictures show 2/5 of a whole. Find the different fractions that are equivalent to 2/5 and write your fractions below each image. 2/5 = 4/10 = ___ = ___ = ___/50 = ___/100
steps: The first picture shows 2/5: 2 shaded rows out of 5 equal rows.
The second picture has each row cut into 2 pieces: 5 × 2 = 10 pieces and 2 × 2 = 4 shaded. That is 4/10, and it is given.
In the third picture cut each row into 3 pieces: 5 × 3 = 15 pieces and 2 × 3 = 6 shaded. The fraction is 6/15.
In the fourth picture cut each row into 4 pieces: 5 × 4 = 20 pieces and 2 × 4 = 8 shaded. The fraction is 8/20.
For ___/50, 5 × 10 = 50, so multiply the top by 10 too: 2 × 10 = 20. The fraction is 20/50.
For ___/100, 5 × 20 = 100, so multiply the top by 20 too: 2 × 20 = 40. The fraction is 40/100.
Check: each bottom number is 5 times a number and each top number is 2 times the same number. For 40/100, 100 ÷ 5 = 20 and 2 × 20 = 40.
items.answer: Sample answer: 2/5 = 4/10 = 6/15 = 8/20 = 20/50 = 40/100. The two open blanks may be other equivalent fractions, but the two boxes must be 20 and 40. Your answer may differ.

videos.answer: Sample answer: 2/5 = 4/10 = 6/15 = 8/20 = 20/50 = 40/100. The two open blanks may be other equivalent fractions, but the two boxes must be 20 and 40. Your answer may differ.

items.question: Fill in the blanks with equivalent fractions. There may be more than one answer. (a): 1/7 = ___; (b): 2/3 = ___; (c): 3/4 = ___; (d): 3/5 = ___
steps: To make an equivalent fraction, multiply the top and the bottom by the same number. Here every part is cut into 2 pieces.

Check: in each answer the bottom number is 2 times the bottom number in the question, and the top number is 2 times the top number in the question. Any other number to multiply by, such as 3, also works.

source: Let Us Do (equivalent fractions), Q2

items.question: Put a tick against the fractions that are equivalent. (a): 2/3 and 3/4; (b): 3/5 and 6/10; (c): 4/12 and 2/6; (d): 6/9 and 1/3
steps: Two fractions are equivalent if one top and bottom are multiplied by the same number to give the other top and bottom.
(a): For 2/3 and 3/4, write both with 12 parts. 2/3 = 8/12 because 2 × 4 = 8 and 3 × 4 = 12. 3/4 = 9/12 because 3 × 3 = 9 and 4 × 3 = 12. 8/12 and 9/12 are different, so no tick.
(d): For 6/9 and 1/3, 1 × 3 = 3 and 3 × 3 = 9, so 1/3 = 3/9. 3/9 is not 6/9, so no tick.
Check: the ticks are on the two pairs where the same number multiplied both the top and the bottom.
items.answer: The ticks go on (b), 3/5 and 6/10, and on (c), 4/12 and 2/6. The pairs in (a) and (d) are not equivalent.

videos.answer: The ticks go on (b), 3/5 and 6/10, and on (c), 4/12 and 2/6. The pairs in (a) and (d) are not equivalent.

source: Let Us Do (equivalent fractions), Q3

items.question: Fill in the boxes such that the fractions become equivalent. (a): 2/5 = ___/10; (b): 3/4 = ___/16; (c): 4/7 = 8/___; (d): 5/9 = 25/___
steps: In each pair, find the number that takes one number to the other, then multiply the other number by it too.
(a): For 2/5 = ___/10, the bottom went from 5 to 10, and 5 × 2 = 10. So the top is 2 × 2 = 4.
(b): For 3/4 = ___/16, the bottom went from 4 to 16, and 4 × 4 = 16. So the top is 3 × 4 = 12.
(c): For 4/7 = 8/___, the top went from 4 to 8, and 4 × 2 = 8. So the bottom is 7 × 2 = 14.
(d): For 5/9 = 25/___, the top went from 5 to 25, and 5 × 5 = 25. So the bottom is 9 × 5 = 45.
